problem: Operator, 2026-11-15, after testing the Watch tab: 'I can only see if an agent is working by the grey string, which is not very indicative of what's happening.' Grounding, master fa3fecb: WatchTab.tsx:94-97 draws the state as plain text in .aw-watch-status (panel-tabs.css:145, color var(--text-2)), preceded by .aw-watch-live, a 7px green dot with a static ring (panel-tabs.css:146), only when working. 'Waiting for your answer' (watchModel.ts:10-19), the state that most needs the operator, has no colour or mark at all, and idle and waiting look identical. The app already has liveness cues to match: the pulsing .aw-pill[data-live] / @keyframes aw-live (story.css:47-52) and task-live-pulse (index.css:2136), and a global prefers-reduced-motion rule (index.css ~2120).

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-15: grey text does not say what is happening. Waiting currently looks the same as idle, yet it is the one state that needs the operator.
requirements.statement: The Watch tab's status line shows each state in its own colour with a mark beside it: working in the app's green, waiting for your answer in the app's amber, idle in a muted neutral. The three states cannot be confused with colour alone or with the text alone.

requirements.rationale: Motion is what says 'something is happening now' at a glance; a different rhythm for waiting keeps it from reading as work in progress.
requirements.statement: While the watched agent is working, its mark pulses continuously; while it is waiting for your answer, its mark draws attention with a slower, distinct pulse; idle has no motion. When the state changes, the colour and motion change with it, without a reload.
The agent menu's entries show each agent's state in the same colour as the status line, so the operator can see who is working or waiting before choosing whom to watch.

requirements.rationale: Accessibility, and the app already honours it everywhere else (index.css's prefers-reduced-motion rule).
requirements.statement: With the operating system's reduce-motion setting on, the marks keep their colours but do not pulse.

in_scope: The Watch tab's status line: a colour and a mark per state (working, waiting for your answer, idle)
Motion for working and waiting, none for idle
The agent menu's per-agent state detail using the same colours
non_goals: Any change to how the state is derived (watchModel.ts stays as it is)
Sounds, notifications or badges outside the Watch tab
Animating the watched conversation's timeline itself
New colour tokens: existing ones only

summary: The Watch tab's 'X is working / idle / waiting for your answer' line is grey text with, at most, a small static green dot. Each state gets its own colour, and working and waiting get motion, so the operator can tell at a glance, from across the screen, what the watched agent is doing.
